page: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 208 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 104 physical cores of Intel Xeon 8280L processors clocked at 2.7 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 105 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 instruction support, 5700 GB of system memory providing 27.4 GB per core, and a bundled 4398 GB local SSD. The instance contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing highlights significant multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing at 187912.86 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 596.36 GB/sec. Memory read operations demonstrate 359.81 GB/sec of uncached bandwidth, contributing to top-tier Redis SET processing reaching 149.33 million operations per second. In contrast, single-core performance ranks in the lower quartile, as evidenced by modest single-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench, and gzip compression metrics.

The resource profile provides strong efficiency for heavy multi-threaded consolidation rather than distributed clusters. With 5.7 TB of RAM and substantial local solid-state storage, this server is specifically suited for memory-bound workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency enterprise data processing, while representing an inefficient fit for single-thread latency-dependent tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure M208ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 208 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 104 physical cores, powered by 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8280L processors. The system delivers 5700 GB of memory, equating to 27.4 GB per core, along with 4398 GB of local SSD storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier multi-threaded computational capabilities, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 187912.86 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 149 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is strong, recording 359.81 GB/sec on large uncached read operations. Conversely, single-thread performance is weak across Geekbench and compression metrics. This profile makes the instance cost-effective and architecturally suited for consolidation of massive in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency enterprise data processing workloads, rather than latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks.
